title: Jeremiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who was Pashur the son of Immer?
questions.explanation: Pashur is identified as the son of Immer, the priest, in Jeremiah 20:1.

questions.question: What did Pashur do to Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet as stated in Jeremiah 20:2.

questions.question: Where was Jeremiah put after being smitten?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was put in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin according to Jeremiah 20:2.

questions.question: What did the LORD rename Pashur?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah tells Pashur that the LORD hath not called him Pashur, but Magormissabib in Jeremiah 20:3.

questions.question: What will happen to Pashur and all that dwell in his house?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesies that Pashur and his household shall go into captivity in Jeremiah 20:6.

questions.question: True or False: Pashur was the chief governor in the house of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Pashur is described as the chief governor in the house of the LORD in Jeremiah 20:1.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was happy about the message he received from the LORD.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah expresses feelings of derision and mockery, indicating his distress, in Jeremiah 20:7-8.

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD made Jeremiah a source of reproach.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah states that the word of the LORD was made a reproach unto him in Jeremiah 20:8.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 20, which event happens first?
questions.explanation: The sequence begins with Pashur smiting Jeremiah before any other event occurs, according to Jeremiah 20:2.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah feel like he could not do?
options: Speak any more in the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Speak any more in the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah said he would not make mention of the LORD or speak any more in His name in Jeremiah 20:9.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah compare the word of the LORD to?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah described the word of the LORD as a burning fire shut up in his bones in Jeremiah 20:9.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah ask the LORD to see?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah asked the LORD to let him see His vengeance on them in Jeremiah 20:12.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah praised the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor from evildoers.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah praises the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor in Jeremiah 20:13.

questions.question: What curse does Jeremiah mention regarding the day he was born?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah curses the day he was born, wishing it not to be blessed in Jeremiah 20:14.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah wish about the man who brought tidings to his father?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah curses the man who brought tidings to his father and made him glad in Jeremiah 20:15.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Pashur do to Jeremiah after hearing his prophecy?
options: He smote him and put him in stocks
questions.correctAnswer: He smote him and put him in stocks
questions.explanation: Pashur smote Jeremiah and put him in the stocks as a punishment for his prophesying, as stated in Jeremiah 20:2.

questions.question: What name did the LORD give to Pashur through Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: The LORD declared that Pashur's name would no longer be Pashur but Magormissabib, indicating a change in his fate as explained in Jeremiah 20:3.

questions.question: According to the LORD, what would happen to Pashur and his friends?
options: They would become a terror to themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They would become a terror to themselves
questions.explanation: The LORD said He would make Pashur a terror to himself and his friends, as stated in Jeremiah 20:4.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah express about his feelings towards the Lord in verse 7?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah expresses that he feels deceived by the Lord, indicating his struggle with his prophetic calling in Jeremiah 20:7.

questions.question: What is the reason Jeremiah cries out violence and spoil?
options: The word of the LORD has become a reproach
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD has become a reproach
questions.explanation: Jeremiah states that he cries out violence and spoil because the word of the LORD was made a reproach unto him, as mentioned in Jeremiah 20:8.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah compare the word of the Lord to in his heart?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah compares the word of the Lord in his heart to a burning fire shut up in his bones, as noted in Jeremiah 20:9.

questions.question: What did Jeremiah's familiars watch for regarding him?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's familiars were watching for his halting, hoping to take revenge on him, as described in Jeremiah 20:10.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah believed that his persecutors would prevail against him.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah affirms that the LORD is with him and that his persecutors shall not prevail, as stated in Jeremiah 20:11.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah ask the LORD to see in verse 12?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah asks the LORD to see His vengeance on his enemies, highlighting his plea for justice in Jeremiah 20:12.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah praises the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor from evildoers.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah praises the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers, as expressed in Jeremiah 20:13.

questions.question: What curse does Jeremiah pronounce regarding the day he was born?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah curses the day he was born, expressing deep sorrow and regret, as seen in Jeremiah 20:14.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah wish about the man who brought tidings of his birth to his father?
options: To be like cities overthrown by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To be like cities overthrown by the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah wishes for that man to be like the cities which the LORD overthrew as a sign of judgment, as stated in Jeremiah 20:16.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah felt that his existence was filled with joy and purpose.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah felt his existence was filled with labor and sorrow, expressing a sense of despair regarding his life, as noted in Jeremiah 20:18.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 20.

questions.question: What name did the LORD give to Pashur instead of his own name?
questions.explanation: The LORD changed Pashur's name to 'Magormissabib' as a sign of the terror that would come upon him and his friends, as stated in Jeremiah 20:3.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 20:4, what did the LORD say He would do to Pashur and his friends?
questions.explanation: The LORD said He would make Pashur a terror to himself and all his friends, as mentioned in Jeremiah 20:4.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 20:6, what fate is prophesied for Pashur and those in his house?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied that Pashur and all those in his house would go into captivity, as stated in Jeremiah 20:6.

questions.question: Jeremiah expresses feeling deceived by the LORD in which verse?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 20:7, Jeremiah states that he feels deceived by the LORD, indicating his struggle with his prophetic calling.

questions.question: What emotion does Jeremiah express about the word of the LORD in Jeremiah 20:9?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah describes the word of the LORD as a 'burning fire shut up in my bones', indicating the compulsion to speak it, as seen in Jeremiah 20:9.

questions.question: What do Jeremiah's familiars hope for regarding him in Jeremiah 20:10?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's familiars watched for his halting, hoping to take revenge on him, as noted in Jeremiah 20:10.

questions.question: The LORD is described as what in Jeremiah 20:11?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 20:11, the LORD is referred to as a 'mighty terrible one', indicating His power and protection over Jeremiah.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah curse in Jeremiah 20:14?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah curses the day he was born, expressing deep sorrow over his existence, as stated in Jeremiah 20:14.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah wish for the man who brought news of his birth in Jeremiah 20:15?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah curses the man who brought news of his birth, indicating his profound distress, as seen in Jeremiah 20:15.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah wish regarding his mother in Jeremiah 20:17?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah expresses a desire that his mother had been barren, wishing he had never been born, as stated in Jeremiah 20:17.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah sings praises to the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor in Jeremiah 20:13.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah sings praises to the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor from evildoers, as highlighted in Jeremiah 20:13.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was pleased with the life he lived according to Jeremiah 20:18.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah expresses sorrow over his life, questioning why he came forth to see labor and sorrow, as stated in Jeremiah 20:18.

questions.question: Which theme in Jeremiah 20 relates to the concept of prophetic suffering found in the New Testament?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's lamentation over his prophetic calling and the mockery he faces parallels the New Testament theme of suffering for righteousness' sake, as seen in Matthew 5:10.

questions.question: The Hebrew word 'Magormissabib' translates to what significant theme in Jeremiah 20?
questions.explanation: 'Magormissabib' can be interpreted to mean 'terror on every side', reflecting the judgment that God pronounced on Pashur, as explained in Jeremiah 20:3.

questions.question: What literary device does Jeremiah use when he expresses the desire for his birth to be cursed?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's intense expressions of wishing his birth to be cursed are examples of hyperbole, emphasizing his deep despair and sorrow, as found in Jeremiah 20:14.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What name did Jeremiah say the LORD had given to Pashur?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:3 states that the LORD hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magormissabib, indicating a divine change of identity.

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD declare would befall Pashur and his household?
options: They would be killed by the sword
They would be buried in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:6 indicates that Pashur and all that dwell in his house shall go into captivity, demonstrating God's judgment upon him.

questions.question: Which emotion does Jeremiah express in relation to his prophetic calling?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 20:14, Jeremiah curses the day he was born, indicating a deep sense of despair regarding his calling as a prophet.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah feel compelled to do despite his anguish?
options: Speak the word of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Speak the word of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:9 reveals that even though he contemplated not speaking any more in God's name, he could not contain the word of the LORD as it was like a burning fire in his bones.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah request from the LORD regarding his enemies?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 20:12, Jeremiah asks the LORD to see His vengeance on his enemies, showing his desire for divine justice.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by His ability to deliver the poor from evildoers?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:13 praises the LORD for delivering the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers, showcasing His justice in protecting the oppressed.

questions.question: What does the name 'Magormissabib' mean in the context of Jeremiah 20?
questions.explanation: The name 'Magormissabib' signifies 'terror on every side', as stated in Jeremiah 20:3, reflecting the impending judgment and fear facing Pashur.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah describe the reaction of his friends to his prophecies?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:7 reveals that Jeremiah feels mocked daily, indicating the derision he faces from those around him.

questions.question: What is the ultimate fate of Pashur according to the LORD's prophecy?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:6 clearly states that Pashur shall come to Babylon and there he shall die, indicating the finality of God's judgment against him.

questions.question: What theological insight can be drawn from Jeremiah's lament in verses 14-18?
options: The futility of life without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: The futility of life without purpose
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:14-18 expresses deep lament about life filled with sorrow and shame, highlighting the futility of existence without divine purpose.

questions.question: Which verse illustrates God's presence as a source of strength for Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:11 states, 'But the LORD is with me as a mighty terrible one', showcasing God's strength and support amidst persecution.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah accuse God of in his lament?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:7 expresses his feeling of being deceived by the LORD, indicating his struggle with understanding God's plan amidst suffering.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 4-5 and verse 11 convey about God's sovereignty?
options: God delivers those who are faithful
God allows suffering for a greater purpose
God does not intervene in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God allows suffering for a greater purpose
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:4-5 and 11 together convey the idea that God's sovereignty includes the allowance of suffering, which ultimately serves His divine purposes.

questions.question: What does the chapter reveal about the nature of prophetic ministry as experienced by Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Throughout Jeremiah 20, the chapter reveals the opposition and suffering Jeremiah faced as a prophet, illustrating the challenging nature of prophetic ministry.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about the suffering of His prophets. What does Jeremiah 20:11-13 actually teach?
options: God is unaware of their trials
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 20:11-13 teaches that despite suffering, God is with His prophets as a mighty one, empowering them to endure and ultimately deliverance will come.
